title: Uniqueness of the scalar-defect class for one algebra
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $A$ a finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebra, and $x,y\in H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(\operatorname{Gal}(K^s/K),(K^s)^\times)$. If $A$ realizes both $x$ and $y$ in the matrix scalar-defect relation [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect], then $x=y$.

source.place: Section 03R1, scalar-defect construction following Lemma 03R6 and preceding Theorem 03R7; Section 0DVG

proof.text: Unpack the two realizations into e,e', positive sizes d,d', locally constant lifts b,b', and homogeneous cocycles z,z'. The two split algebras have the same vector-space dimension, so d^2=(d')^2 and positivity gives d=d'. Reindex and apply Skolem-Noether to the change of splitting, obtaining a fixed invertible matrix P with e'(a)=P^{-1}e(a)P.

Put d(g)=P^{-1}b(g)g(P). Compute that it implements the same descent datum for e' as b'(g). The elements e'(1 tensor a) span the full matrix algebra over Ks, so the quotient b'(g)d(g)^{-1} commutes with every matrix. It is a unique scalar unit c(g). The entries of P lie in a finite separable extension, hence g(P) is locally constant. Therefore d is locally constant, and extracting c from a fixed diagonal entry of the quotient proves c is locally constant; the size is positive, so such an entry exists.

Substitute b'(g)=c(g)d(g) in the two multiplication-defect equations and cancel P, g(P), and gh(P). The inhomogeneous values satisfy z'(g,h)=c(g)g(c(h))c(gh)^{-1}z(g,h). Define the homogeneous one-cochain q(g0,g1)=g0(c(g0^{-1}g1)), written additively. It is equivariant and continuous because c is locally constant and the coefficient action is continuous. Its alternating differential has inhomogeneous values z'-z. Equivariance recovers the full homogeneous cochain from these values, so z'-z is this differential. The homology projection kills it. The two recorded image equations then give x=y.
